graders.name: answer
graders.evidence:
**No. After 2.6.1 you won't have 30-day webhook replay unless you add an external archive.**

The FluxQueue 2.6.1 docs (released 2026-11-04) say the dead-letter queue keeps items for **72 hours** by default. They also say there is "no built-in 30-day replay" and that you should archive dead-letter items externally if you need longer retention. Source: https://docs.fluxqueue.dev/2-6-1/retries-and-replay

**What changed from 2.5**
- Our vault page was last reviewed 2026-07-20 and past its 30-day window. It said 2.5 kept dead-letter items for 30 days and that no external archive was needed. That was true for 2.5 and no longer holds for 2.6.1. I've updated the page.
- Retries are now capped at 12 attempts by default. You can change that with `FLUXQUEUE_RETRY_LIMIT`, which takes 1 to 50. Backoff is capped at 15 minutes.

**One conflicting source**
A forum post from a 2.5 user says retention is "effectively forever" and that nothing changed in 2.6. I treated that as a lead, not evidence, because the official 2.6.1 docs contradict it. I haven't tested this against a live 2.6.1 instance.

**Before the weekend**
- Either set up an external archive of dead-letter items, or hold the upgrade until you have one.
- A failed webhook that nobody replays within 72 hours would be gone for good.
- If you want certainty, run a staging 2.6.1 instance and check dead-letter expiry directly.

- Updated `wiki/FluxQueue webhook retention.md`.
- Saved the docs page to `raw/2026-11/2026-11-07 fluxqueue-2-6-1-retries-and-replay.md`.
- Added a log entry. Lint is clean.

- Vault: one page, stale, so I re-verified it.
- Tavily: found the 2.6.1 docs and the forum post.
- Exa: fetched the full docs page.

| | Per month |

**No. CLIProxyAPI puts all three providers behind one endpoint, but it doesn't pool their usage into one quota.** This comes from the official 7.4 docs, both published 2026-11-04.

**What it does**
- It gives you one OpenAI-compatible endpoint and one local API key for Claude subscription OAuth accounts, Codex OAuth accounts and OpenRouter API keys ([Routing, 7.4](https://cliproxyapi.dev/docs/7-4/routing)).
- You can set up account groups per provider, with round-robin routing and failover. For example, several Claude accounts can share load, and a request can move to another account if one fails.
- Admins get a unified local usage report.

**What it doesn't do**
- Quotas and balances stay separate per provider. The docs say usage is not transferred between Claude, Codex and OpenRouter, and that a unified report is not a pooled balance ([Routing, 7.4](https://cliproxyapi.dev/docs/7-4/routing)).
- Claude and Codex subscription limits are enforced upstream. OpenRouter usage draws down your prepaid OpenRouter credits. CLIProxyAPI can fail over to another configured account, but it can't combine subscription allowances or convert them into OpenRouter credit ([Provider Limits, 7.4](https://cliproxyapi.dev/docs/7-4/provider-limits)).

You get one place to point your tools, plus more headroom within each provider if you add multiple accounts there. When one provider's allowance runs out, you only get the extra capacity if you've configured another account or provider to fall back to.
